records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:14 — Concurrent matches use a read-modify-write increment, so overlapping blocked attempts can overwrite each other and silently undercount abuse activity.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in the `should_block?` method at lines 11-17 of blocked_email.rb. The code does `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save`, which is a classic read-modify-write pattern. If two concurrent requests check the same blocked email, both could read the same match_count value, increment it locally, and save - resulting in only one increment being recorded instead of two. This is a real concurrency bug that could cause undercounting of blocked email attempts.

records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — Exact email matching without case normalization lets a blocked address evade registration blocking by changing domain capitalization.
records.rationale: The diff shows `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 performs an exact string match. In most databases, this is case-sensitive by default. The code stores and queries emails without any case normalization (no `downcase` or similar). This means if 'bad@SPAMMERS.org' is blocked, a user could register with 'bad@spammers.org' and bypass the block. This is a real correctness/security defect in the email blocking logic.
